text.p: French lead and zinc producer Metaleurop said its 600 million franc capital increase announced earlier this month would involve the issue of 7.6 million shares with warrants attached at a price of 79.10 francs.
The issue, which began on March 18 and will end on March 24, could be raised to 660 million francs, it said in a newspaper notice.
Each share will carry one warrant.
Metaleurop was down 2.71 percent at 0933 GMT, trading at 75.40 francs.
Existing shareholders will have the right to subscribe to two shares, with warrant attached, for every five shares held.
Two warrants will give the right to subscribe to a Metaleurop share at a price of 79.10 francs. The warrants can be exercised from April 2, 1997 to April 2, 2000.
Metaleurop said the issue followed cumulative losses of 708 million francs over the past five fiscal years.
The shares will have a nominal 25 franc value.
The notice said that main shareholders German group Preussag and Swiss-based Glencore, will participate in the issue in proportion to their respective 25.4 percent stakes.
Preussag has 40.48 percent of Metaleurop voting rights and Glencore 20.24 percent.
The notice also said that Glencore might over the next twelve months seek to increase its stake in Metaleurop
